title: AMPSphere & APEX Deep Learning Mine Global Microbiomes & Extinct Species for Novel Antibiotics
aiSystem: Macrel & APEX Deep Learning Peptide Miners (UPenn / Fudan / QUT)
whyItMatters: Deep learning mined 63,410 global metagenomes (863,498 antimicrobial peptides) and extinct species proteomes (including woolly mammoths), discovering potent preclinical antibiotics validated in mouse infection models.
summary: Published in back-to-back landmark June 2024 studies in Cell (June 5) and Nature Biomedical Engineering (June 11) led by César de la Fuente-Nunez at the University of Pennsylvania with Luis Pedro Coelho (Fudan / QUT), Célio Dias Santos-Júnior, Fangping Wan, and Marcelo D. T. Torres, machine-learning peptide discovery pipelines unlocked two vast unexplored reservoirs of antibiotics. In AMPSphere (Cell), ML surveyed 63,410 global metagenomes and 87,920 microbial genomes to catalog 863,498 non-redundant candidate antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), with 79 of 100 synthesized peptides killing pathogens in vitro and leading hits matching polymyxin B in mice. Days later in Nature Biomedical Engineering, the recurrent-attention deep learning model APEX mined >10.3 million peptides across all known extinct organisms ('molecular de-extinction'), yielding active preclinical antibiotics including mammuthusin-2 (woolly mammoth), hydrodamin-1 (ancient sea cow), and mylodonin-2 (giant sloth) with confirmed efficacy in mouse infection models.
technicalHighlights: AMPSphere (Cell) uncovered 863,498 candidate antimicrobial peptides across 63,410 global metagenomes; 79% of 100 synthesized candidates showed antibacterial activity.
APEX (Nature Biomedical Engineering) used a recurrent-attention deep neural network to mine 10,311,899 peptides from extinct proteomes, identifying 11,035 candidates absent from extant species.

Validated top metagenomic (e.g., lachnospirin-1, enterococcin-1) and de-extinct (e.g., mammuthusin-2, elephasin-2) peptides in vivo in murine skin-abscess and thigh-infection models against drug-resistant pathogens.
caveats: Antimicrobial peptides face known clinical translation barriers including proteolytic degradation, systemic toxicity, and manufacturing cost; candidates remain preclinical pending IND-enabling toxicology and human trials.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated AI mining of planetary metagenomes and extinct evolutionary proteomes as systematic new paradigms for antibiotic discovery.
scoreRationale.ripple: Created AMPSphere—a massive open global resource of ~863K candidate peptides—and launched molecular de-extinction as a mainstream drug-discovery strategy.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Cell and Nature Biomedical Engineering with wet-lab chemical synthesis of >160 peptides and in vivo murine infection validation.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed years of conventional natural-product bioassay screening across tens of thousands of ecosystems into computational screening followed by targeted synthesis.
